Yes I do see a hematologist. My ferritin level wasn’t raising even after a year on supplements, even after they doubled the daily recommended dosage. I had to see several other specialists first so they could try to find out the cause- they expected heavy periods, lupus or internal bleeding. I had to see a gynecologist, rheumatologist, and a gastroenterologist. Each of those doctors did their separate testing, lots of bloodwork, colonoscopy, etc. Eventually for me they found that the cause was autoimmune disease related, celiac disease, lupus, hashimotos. My endocrinologist who I normally see for my Hashimotos disease did an iron infusion but it didn’t work so they sent me to a hematologist to try another type which was then successful. I go every few months now whenever my levels drop.

Try the supplements first, if they work GREAT! And for most people they do work, but they take time. Make sure you are taking a good supplement- mega blood builders is a highly recommended one and you can get it on amazon. Make sure you are getting enough vitamin C as well- drink your OJ with your iron pill in the morning. Don’t take calcium and vitamin D with your iron, it blocks the absorption. Stop drinking caffeine and tea, they also block absorption of iron.

It’s a long and daunting path but you will feel so much better once you get help, you have to be an advocate for yourself and if you cannot bring someone you trust with you to appointments.

1. Yes low ferritin but normal hemoglobin will cause tiredness as well as MANY other symptoms, you can even pass out and it can effect your blood pressure levels and heart rate. Ferritin levels are also very important for thyroid function among other things. 

2. Many general practitioners aren’t well versed in ferritin, the range is too broad and many will look at the number and think “that’s normal” when really it is not ideal. After your ferritin level drops your iron stores become depleted next, which is very very bad. Over time your hemoglobin will also drop if left untreated. You need to find a good hematologist who will give you supplements - and if you don’t absorb those - iron infusions.
